Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant journey you've been on, becoming a new mother, and I'm here to support you every step of the way. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and if there are any areas where we can offer additional support during this postpartum period.

The EPDS is designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a valuable tool in our clinical assessment. It's completely confidential, and everything we discuss today will remain between us. I want you to feel safe and supported throughout our conversation. My goal is to create a space where you feel comfortable sharing your thoughts and feelings, without any judgment.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand your emotional well-being over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll be here to listen and support you throughout the process. Your responses will help me better understand your postpartum experience and identify any areas where you might need additional support or resources.

So, let's get started. Here's my first question: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, it's been really tough for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to be a pretty cheerful person, but since having the baby, it feels like that part of me has been missing. I do still enjoy some things, like watching my baby smile or seeing them discover new things, but it's just not the same as it used to be. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and even when I do laugh, it doesn't feel as genuine as it used to. It's like, I'll be playing with the baby, and they'll do something cute, and I'll laugh, but then I'll just start feeling overwhelmed and worried about everything again. Like, am I doing this right? Is the baby healthy? Am I a good mom? Those thoughts just creep in and it's hard for me to shake them off. So, to answer your question, I guess I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, but it's just not as often as it used to be, and it doesn't feel as carefree.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) Yeah, like I said, it's just not the same as it used to be. I feel like I'm just pretending to be happy sometimes, you know? Like, I'll be laughing and smiling on the outside, but inside, I'm still feeling really anxious and worried. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I feel like I'm just so tired all the time, and I don't know how to keep up with everything. I'm just trying to survive each day, you know? And when I do have those moments where I can laugh and see the funny side of things, it's just... it's fleeting. It doesn't last. And then I'm back to feeling overwhelmed and guilty, like I'm not doing enough for my baby or for myself. (pausing, looking down) Sorry, I don't know, it's just... it's hard to explain. (starting to tear up)
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head) Not really... I mean, I used to love doing things, like going out with friends, or trying new restaurants, or just taking a relaxing bath. But now, it all just feels like so much work. And even when I do try to do something I used to enjoy, it's just not the same. I'll be thinking about the baby the whole time, worrying about whether they're okay, or if they need me. And even when my partner is taking care of them, I'll just be sitting there, feeling anxious, thinking about all the things that could go wrong. (sighing) It's hard to explain, but it's like, I just don't feel like myself anymore. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, trying to be a good mom, but not really enjoying anything. And when I do try to look forward to things, like a walk with the baby, or a coffee with a friend, I just end up feeling guilty, like I'm leaving the baby, or like I'm not doing enough. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) It's like, I've lost myself in all of this...
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Oh, yeah... all the time. I feel like I'm just one mistake away from being a terrible mother. If the baby cries, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If they're not sleeping, I think it's because I'm not establishing a good routine. If they're not eating, I think it's because I'm not making enough milk. It's like, everything is my fault, and I just can't seem to get anything right. (voice cracking) And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, if I forget to burp the baby, or if I don't change their diaper quickly enough... I just feel like I'm failing all the time. (wiping away tears) And it's hard, because my partner is always trying to reassure me, telling me that I'm doing a great job, but it's just hard for me to believe that. I feel like I'm just pretending to be a mom, and that someday, someone is going to figure out that I have no idea what I'm doing. (shaking head) It's a really hard feeling to shake, the feeling of guilt and self-doubt. It's just always there, lurking in the back of my mind.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(exhaling deeply) Yes... all the time. I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll think, "What if they choke?" or "What if they're not getting enough milk?" And then I'll start to worry about all the things that could go wrong, and it just spirals out of control. (rubbing temples) I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll think, "What if the baby stops breathing?" or "What if there's a fire in the house?" And I'll get up and check on the baby, like, five times, just to make sure they're okay. (laughing nervously) It's ridiculous, I know, but I just can't seem to shake these thoughts. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I'll worry about my partner, or my other family members, or just the world in general. It's like, my mind is just constantly racing, and I don't know how to turn it off. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I feel like I'm going crazy, like I'm just losing my grip on reality. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sorry, it's just... it's hard to explain. It's just this constant feeling of anxiety, like I'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, eyes welling up with tears) Yes... that happens to me a lot. I'll be sitting there, just doing something normal, like feeding the baby or changing their diaper, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like, my body is responding to some kind of threat, but there's no threat there. It's just... my mind, I guess. (taking a deep breath) It's hard to explain, but it's like, I'll be feeling fine, and then suddenly I'll think, "What if something happens to the baby?" or "What if I'm not a good enough mom?" And then I'll start to feel this panic rising up, and it's hard to calm myself down. (wiping away tears) Sometimes I'll try to distract myself, like by watching TV or going for a walk, but it doesn't always work. The panic just... it just feels like it's always lurking there, waiting to pounce. (looking down, voice shaking) And it's scary, because I don't know how to control it. I feel like I'm just at the mercy of these feelings, and it's really frightening. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sorry... it's just... it's hard to talk about this stuff.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling a sense of relief that someone understands) Oh, yes... that's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner... it all just feels so overwhelming. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, remembering to buy diapers, or scheduling doctor's appointments, or just keeping track of everything. It's like, my brain is just constantly spinning, trying to keep up with it all. (sighing) And sometimes I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. Like, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll think, "Okay, I've got this. I can do this." But then something else will come up, like a mess in the kitchen, or a phone call from a family member, and it's just like... (throwing hands up in the air) I don't know, it just feels like everything is too much for me. (looking down, feeling tears well up in eyes) And it's hard, because I feel like I should be able to handle it all. I feel like I should be this capable, competent mom, but really, I just feel like I'm struggling to keep my head above water. (voice cracking) Sorry... it's just... it's really hard to admit that I'm not doing okay.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of recognition) Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. I mean, that's part of it, but it's also... (sighing) it's just my mind, I guess. I'll be lying in bed, and I'll start thinking about all the things that are worrying me, like the baby's health, or my relationship with my partner, or just... everything. And I'll start to feel this anxiety creeping in, and it's hard to calm myself down. (rubbing eyes) I'll try to relax, I'll try to breathe deeply, but my mind just won't shut off. And then I'll start to feel this sadness, this overwhelming sense of unhappiness, and it's just... (shaking head) it's hard to explain. It's like, I'll be feeling fine, and then suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me, and it's hard to shake it off. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I'll lie in bed for hours, just staring at the ceiling, feeling like I'm the only one who's awake, and it's just... it's a really lonely feeling. (pausing, taking a deep breath) And it's not just at night, either. I'll be feeling unhappy during the day, too, and it's just... it's hard to explain. It's like, I'll be doing something normal, like feeding the baby or playing with them, and suddenly I'll just feel this sadness, this sense of overwhelm, and it's hard to keep going. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) Sorry... it's just... it's really hard to talk about this stuff.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a lump in throat) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I know I'm supposed to be happy, I'm a new mom, I have a beautiful baby... but it's just... (sighing) it's not that simple. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'll be taking care of the baby, and I'll be smiling and laughing, but inside, I'm just feeling so empty and sad. (looking down, voice cracking) It's like, I'll be holding the baby, and I'll be thinking, "I love you so much," but at the same time, I'll be feeling this overwhelming sense of sadness and despair. It's like, my heart is just heavy all the time, and I don't know how to make it feel better. (wiping away tears) Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll just start crying, and I won't even know why. It's just... (shaking head) it's like, my emotions are just all over the place, and I don't know how to control them. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this happy, capable mom, but really, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together. (voice barely above a whisper) Sorry... it's just... it's really hard to admit this, but I feel like I'm just really struggling right now.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, feeling a sense of relief that someone understands) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of emotion wash over me, and I'll just start crying. It's not just when something's wrong, either. It's like, I'll be happy, and then suddenly I'll just feel this sadness, and I'll start crying. (wiping away tears) It's really frustrating, because I feel like I'm just losing control, you know? I'll be in the middle of doing something, like changing the baby's diaper, or making lunch, and I'll just start crying. And it's not just a little bit of crying, either. It's like, I'll be sobbing, and I won't be able to stop. (looking down, feeling embarrassed) It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this strong, capable mom, but really, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together. (sighing) I've been crying a lot at night, too, when the baby's asleep. It's like, I'll be lying in bed, and I'll just start thinking about everything, and I'll start crying. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) It's just... it's really hard, you know? I feel like I'm just so overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it stop. (voice cracking) Sorry... it's just... it's really hard to talk about this.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pauses, looking down, feeling a sense of shame and vulnerability) Yes... I've had those thoughts. (pauses again, taking a deep breath) It's not something I'm proud of, and it's not something I've ever thought about before having the baby. But lately, when things get really overwhelming, and I feel like I'm just not doing anything right... (trails off, struggling to find the words) I've had thoughts about... about not being here anymore. (looks up, eyes welling up with tears) It's not that I want to hurt myself, it's just that sometimes it feels like it would be easier if I just... wasn't here. (pauses again, feeling a sense of shame and guilt) I know that's not a healthy way to think, and I'm ashamed to even admit it. But it's the truth. (looks down, feeling a sense of vulnerability) I've never acted on those thoughts, and I don't think I would. But they're there, lurking in the back of my mind, and it's scary. (pauses again, taking a deep breath) I just feel like I'm drowning in all of this, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. (looks up, eyes pleading for help) I just want to feel better. I want to be a good mom, and a good person, and I don't want to have these thoughts anymore.

The patient also expresses feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and self-doubt, particularly in regards to their ability to care for their baby. **Reasoning:** The patient's responses indicate a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med> and <med>anxiety</med>. They report persistent feelings of <sym>sadness</sym>, <sym>loss of pleasure</sym>, and <sym>anxiety</sym>, which are impacting their daily functioning and ability to care for their baby. The patient's thoughts of self-harm are a significant safety concern, and immediate follow-up and support are necessary to ensure their safety and well-being. According to the <med>Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)</med> guidelines, a score of 25 indicates a high possibility of <med>depression</med>. The patient's symptoms also align with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med>
2. Encourage <med>sleep hygiene practices</med> to improve sleep quality
3. Refer to <med>mental health specialist</med> for further evaluation and support
4. Provide resources for <med>postpartum support groups</med> and <med>online therapy platforms</med>
5. Emphasize the importance of self-care and stress management techniques, such as <med>deep breathing exercises</med> and <med>meditation</med>
6. Encourage open communication with partner and family members about feelings and concerns
